lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: identification and official records

objective: Learners build a general 'which record category might this need' checklist and apply it to six hypothetical situations, so they practice the pattern of anticipating documentation needs while explicitly deferring the specifics to a current, official local source.
scenario: Given four generic record categories (a government-issued ID, school records, health records, proof of address) and six hypothetical situations (renting a room, opening a certain kind of account, applying for a certain kind of job, traveling, a medical appointment, registering for something), the learner matches likely categories to each situation and explicitly flags that the exact requirements must be verified with a current local or official source, not assumed from this worksheet.
safetyNotes: This lesson names general categories only; it does not assert what any specific real institution actually requires, since that varies by place and changes over time.
Every match includes an explicit note to verify against a current local or official source before relying on it for a real situation.
materials: the provided four record categories and six hypothetical situations

tasks.directions: Before matching, guess which of the six situations would need the most different record categories.

prompts.text: Of the six hypothetical situations, which do you guess would require the most different kinds of records, and why?

tasks.directions: Match likely record categories to each of the six situations.

prompts.text: I matched at least one likely record category to each of the six situations.
For every match, I wrote 'verify with a current local/official source' rather than stating it as certain.

tasks.directions: Explain your reasoning for the two situations you found trickiest to match.

prompts.text: Pick the two situations that were hardest to match, and explain what made them harder and how you resolved it.

tasks.directions: Reflect on the limits of this worksheet.

prompts.text: Why can't this worksheet just tell you exactly what you'd need for each real situation?

remediation: If the learner states any match as a certain fact rather than something to verify (for example, asserting exactly what a real institution requires), reteach the distinction between 'a plausible category to check' and 'a verified requirement,' then have them revise the phrasing.
extension: Have the learner add a seventh, self-invented hypothetical situation and match it the same way.
